Two independent safety nets keep it from ever depending on the ~50-100 Neurons/image estimate holding exactly: a hard DAILY_IMAGE_CAP=60 count-based ceiling well under the estimated free budget, and reactive handling of Cloudflare's own quota/rate-limit rejection if it happens anyway (same pattern pipeline/quota_guard.py already uses for YouTube's quota) -- either one falls back to Pixabay rather than failing the run. pipeline/assemble.py: added a real Ken Burns pan (not just center-zoom) for AI-sourced clips specifically -- the crop window's focal point now drifts toward a randomly-chosen corner/edge as the existing zoompan zooms in, instead of staying centered. Pixabay clips keep the unchanged plain center-zoom (they already have their own camera/subject motion; stacking an artificial pan on top of real motion isn't obviously an improvement). Caught and fixed a real bug before committing: the naive pan math put the crop window out of bounds at this pipeline's modest zoom levels (verified numerically: at zoom_end=1.15, a pan target of 0.85 needs the crop's left edge at 41.5% but the valid range tops out at 13.0%) -- fixed by clamping the x/y expressions to the valid crop range directly in the ffmpeg expression (min/max), so any pan target is safe regardless of zoom level rather than needing hand-derived per-zoom-level-safe values
.github/workflows/produce-upload.yml / README.md: wired CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN through as new optional secrets
